features.text: The patient has numbness and tingling in the fingers and pain in the wrist.
The patient has had pain and numbness in the right wrist and hand for several months.
The patient's symptoms started on their own and are mostly noticed at night.
The patient wakes up with numb hands and needs to shake them out.
The patient experiences numbness in the fingers.
The patient has weakness in the left hand.
The patient has difficulty feeling and drops things due to reduced sensation.
The patient does not have any problems with the right hand.
The patient drinks a beer or two on Fridays and Saturdays.
The patient does not have any known allergies or medical conditions mentioned.
The patient works in landscaping, involving heavy labor and repetitive movements.
The patient experiences a jolt or zing in the fingertips when the doctor taps the right wrist.
The patient experiences the same jolt or zing in the fingertips when the doctor taps the left wrist.
The patient feels a little more weird on the thumb side than the pointer finger side when the doctor touches the fingers on the right.
The patient prefers to delegate some tasks to other employees.
